claims.text: Program.cs at stage-4 reads one database connection string, GetConnectionString("Default") (the other, "Redis", is for the cache), and passes it to both AddCatalogModule and AddDonHangInfrastructure; no replica connection exists.

consistency-per-operation.md: at stage-4 the API does not read db-replica, has one connection string pointing at the primary; the replica receives changes asynchronously, so a read there may miss the caller's own write.

Allowed to move: the product list, because it accepts slightly old data and writes nothing back from its result. The table row for the list says it reads the primary each time only because the code has no other copy.

Not moved: own order and its history, any read right after the caller's write, a single product read through ProductCache (also when ordering): a reload from a lagging replica would put the old price back into Redis for a whole TTL (5 minutes, table row 1).
Orders placed while a stale price sits in ProductCache use the old price, at most 5 minutes; moving any other operation to the replica requires changing the table first.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/consistency-per-operation.md lines 21-29 (Giá lúc đặt đơn), 53 @ stage-4

claims.text: capacity-plan.md: stage-4 keeps every read on the primary, db-replica is lab only; move first the product list; not own orders, order history, reads after the caller's write; trigger: planned product-read peak crosses the primary's headroom (no number given).

Way back: a routed read returns to the primary when the replica lags more than the product list tolerates or does not answer; the replica carries only reads moved to it; stage-4 has no routing code. Neither document says how a read right after the caller's write is recognised.

PostgreSQL streaming replication is asynchronous by default: unless synchronous_standby_names names a standby, the primary commits without waiting for it, so a read on the standby can miss a committed change; the standby continuously applies the WAL it receives.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, 26.2.5 Streaming Replication; 26.2.8 Synchronous Replication (synchronous_standby_names empty by default)

claims.text: replica-lag.sh at stage-4 starts db-replica as a fresh copy of db, then: right after UPDATE on db, db returns 1300000 and db-replica 1250000; 6 s later db-replica returns 1300000. The lab replica waits 5 s on purpose before applying each change.

claims.text: Product search (ADR 0030) is not at stage-4; its table row gives it the same choice as the product list, on the primary, replica when capacity-plan.md allows.

Route by operation, not by HTTP method, when some reads must see the caller's own write; keep all reads on the primary until the plan's stated condition holds, because routing adds a connection, a per-query check, a way back and stale answers.

claims.text: If the replica falls behind at the busiest hour, the way back returns the moved reads to the primary at once, so the plan should still check the primary can take them back for a while.
